MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ADJOURNED MEETING
  AUGUST 15, 2022

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 6:06 p.m. at Linden H. Chandler Preserve, 95 Buckskin
  Lane, Rolling Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR CIAROLLA.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR CIAROLLA led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Bain,  Ciarolla,  Persichina,  Romanelli,
  McCormick, and Retz

  Commissioners Absent:  Pope

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas

  Also Present:  Councilmember Stegura

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF JULY 18,
  2022

  VICE CHAR BAIN made a motion, seconded by
  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  JULY 18, 2022.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
August 15, 2022
   A.  CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICES TURF REMOVAL PROJECTS AT CITY HALL
  AND HIGHRIDGE PARK

  Assistant City Manager Davis gave a brief overview of the written report with
  additional information provided by Councilmember Stegura who serves as the
  Environmental Advisory Committee Chair. VICE CHAIR BAIN, as a member of the
  subcommittee, commented that it was a wonderful project to beautify the areas but
  also make them more functional. COUNCILMEMBER STEGURA noted that the
  budget set is coordinated with the CalWater rebate.

  CHAIR CIAROLLA stated concern that decomposed granite can get warm in hot
  weather and there should be consideration of adding trees in areas that will not
  offer shade. VICE CHAIR BAIN stated that trees will be preserved, and some may
  be added to areas.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK described the seating should be natural looking,
  similar to log seating which he recently observed while traveling. COMMISSIONER
  PERSICHINA asked that the plants considered include year-round blooms since
  native plants can often look dry and not colorful. COUNCILMEMBER STEGURA
  responded that the subcommittee agreed and that plants will provide year-round
  blooming but also attract butterflies and hummingbirds and the City is working the
  Palos Verdes Land Conservancy on plant selections and possible future purchase.
  VICE CHAIR BAIN added that the goal is to show different plants in different
  seasons.

  In response to COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, COUNCILMEMBER STEGURA
  explained that a demonstration garden at City Hall is part of the project and VICE
  CHAIR BAIN added that signage will be incorporated as well.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked why the project considered the whole area
  and not smaller portions given the limited dollar amount available. ACM Davis
  explained that the dollar amount provided by CalWater covers the full area and if
  the area is adjusted, the dollars available may be adjusted as well.
  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if there was consideration of approaching
  this project similar to when medians were re-landscaped which was a staged
  approach. COUNCILMEMBER STEGURA responded that the ultimate goal of
  these projects was to save water which addresses the larger, expanded area.

  COMMISSION RETZ shared that some native plants can be harmful to horses so
  suggested that these types of plants be set away from common horse areas like
  the bridle trail and hitching post.

  VICE CHAIR CIAROLLA stated that the Highridge project seemed much more
  functional and not as different visually as City Hall but will make the space look

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
August 15, 2022
   nicer. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI responded that the area has been a concern
  related to drainage.
  COMMISSIONERS agreed to have feedback shared with the City Council at their
  August 23 meeting and to hold a special meeting to review the final plans,
  specifications, and the landscape proposal in advance of the September 13 City
  Council meeting. COUNCILMEMBER STEGURA requested that it be a joint
  special meeting to include the Environmental Advisory Committee as this was an
  important initiative to them.

  No further action was taken.

  B.  CITY CELEBRATION (VERBAL UPDATE)

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the the event
  plans.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if staff and the subcommittee reviewed the
  lessons learned from last year to which Community Services Supervisor affirmed
  those comments were considered in this year’s planning.

  COMMISSION MCCORMICK stated the hayride is very popular and asked if there
  was another tractor to add. ACM Davis stated that there is not access to another
  tractor, but staff would look further into it staff would look further into it to see if it is
  possible.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN explained updates made to the invitation flyer that will be mailed
  to the community.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that any action to clarify the process for
  visitors in flyers and signage is helpful. VICE CHAIR BAIN, as a subcommittee
  member, reported that more volunteers will be needed and that improved signage
  with greater visibility will be added. In response to COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK,
  ACM Davis explained that in addition to the regular barbeque lunch, an additional
  snack station will be available, which will include water, and there will be a food
  truck there with sweets. VICE CHAIR BAIN added that watermelon will be available
  at the snack station.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted that there were problems with the walkie
  talkies that help coordinate staff. He also suggested that if we get low on tickets,
  we can recycle them from the activities.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN noted that pre-sale of wristbands will be helpful.

  7.  STAFF ITEMS

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
August 15, 2022
   A.  ROCKBLUFF PARK (VERBAL REPORT)
  ACM Davis reported that there are additional ADA enhancements needed for the
  pathway and that staff is working with the contractor on the swing structure that was
  installed, which was not the structure approved. She reported that the contractor
  indicated they will cover the labor cost of work but there is a difference in cost of
  the equipment itself.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that the contractor should cover the full cost
  since it was fully their error and the City awarded the contract based on the
  proposed cost provided. COMMISSIONER RETZ echoed his sentiment as did the
  remaining COMMISSIONERS and directed staff to have that conversation with the
  contractor. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI additionally stated concern that the
  pour in play footing could now be compromised with changing out the structures.
  ACM Davis responded that staff is working with the City Attorney and will work out
  a plan to address these issues and return to the COMMISSION if further direction
  or approvals are needed.

  COMMISSIOENR ROMANELLI also asked for more information on a memorial rock
  found at Rockbluff. ACM Davis responded that staff is researching further.

  B.  PICKLEBALL PROGRAM (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the program
  noting the growing interest and that the planned open house has had to be
  postponed to a date uncertain.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked staff to bring back an item related
  cameras in parks.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER RETZ shared that he will be leaving the Commission in the
  next year as he prepares to move out of state.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if Peter Weber Equestrian Center would
  consider an open house to showcase their facility. ACM Davis responded that
  the next Commission meeting will include a tour and we can ask the operator to
  consider something like that.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
August 15, 2022
   9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF JULY 26, 2022.

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  NONE.

  11.  PARK TOURS

  A.  CHANDLER PRESERVE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas shared the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land
  Conservancy report:

  •  Volunteers continue planting PV blue butterfly host plants through the
  adopt-a-plot program
  •  Annual fuel modification fire abatement complete
  •  Monitoring to protect conservation of easements from neighbors of the
  preserve continues

  The Commission then continued to walk through the Preserve.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR CIAROLLA MOVED TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:17 PM TO THE NEXT ADJOURNED
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON SEPTEMBER
  19,2022 AT 6:00 P.M., WHICH BE HELD AT THE CITY HALL COUNCIL
  CHAMBER WITH A TOUR OF PEPPERWOOD PARK AND THE PETER
  WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  ___________________________
  Rosa Pinuelas  Valerie Ciarolla
  Community Services Supervisor  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
August 15, 2022
